definition: Hypnotic induction is the process of guiding a person into a hypnotic or trance-like state by directing attention toward inner experience or the body. In this context, it refers to producing a non-ordinary state of consciousness that may be accompanied by changes in brain activity.

reasons: The packet does not define hypnotic induction as a process of guiding a person into a hypnotic or trance-like state; it only says mind–body interventions may include elements of trance induction and hypnosis while directing focus to the body and inner experiences.

The claim that hypnotic induction refers to producing a non-ordinary state of consciousness is not directly supported; the packet only says such a state may occur during a mind–body intervention and may be similar to hypnotic induction.

The wording presents the brain-activity point as part of the term’s meaning, but the source only reports this as an experimental hypothesis about a mind–body intervention, not as a general definition of hypnotic induction.

The packet describes this as a *hypothesis* in an experimental study (“test the hypothesis that a non-ordinary state of consciousness may occur”), but the definition states definitively that induction “refers to producing” a non-ordinary state.

The packet does not explicitly define hypnotic induction as a “process of guiding a person into” a trance; it instead notes that mind–body interventions “include elements of trance induction and hypnosis” with attention directed to body/inner experience.
